label: input h at original positions 3-5
explanation: Fires only when the input token is the letter h, during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase, at positions 3-5 (and weakly at 2). Every h input at t=3..5 activates (precision 1.0). Magnitude is highest at t=3-4 (~0.9-1.2) and lower at t=5 (examples 0.3-0.45 there); t=2 h occurrences fire weakly and only sometimes (~1% of mass). Does not fire on h at t=0,1 or t>=6, on any other token, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase (even when h is fed back as output). Context tokens, L, and repeat count barely modulate it.

issues: Minor: at t=2, h fires only about 24% of the time (dev precision 0.24 for h & t==2), with tiny magnitudes of about 0.03-0.07 relative to max. That is about 0.9% of activation mass, which matches the 'weak tail' claim. Restricting to longer L did not raise precision (0.23), so it is not a systematic subclass worth adding.
Copy phase: only 1 active step in roughly 2.7M copy steps, and h in phase != 0 has precision about 1e-5. The 'never fires in copy phase' claim is effectively true.

Test split: precision 1.0, 0 false positives, recall 0.911, F1 0.954, mass recall 0.991. All 4003 misses are faint h activations at t=2. No other token, position or length pattern is among the misses.

Profile confirms: zero activation at t=0, t=1 and t>=6, on the delimiter, and on any non-h token. Mass is concentrated at t=3 (0.44) and t=4 (0.40), with less at t=5 (0.14) per similar count, so per-step magnitude is lower at t=5, as claimed.
